    "rationale": "Evidence: the only raced design (iteration 2: sensors at x ±0.04, y 0.04, size 0.012, kp 3.0, kd 0.5, ki 0, base 1.4) finished 0 of 60 trials. Every run ended off track: progress 0.22 on the oval, 0.04 on the s-bend, 0.035 on the slalom. Two facts matter most. First, line_loss_events was 0 in every trial, so the sensors kept reading tape right up to the exit. Edge loss at the outer sensors is therefore not the proximate cause, which weakens critique item 1 as the main failure mode. Second, steering_oscillation (0.066 to 0.115) and max_error (about 0.061, the limit) show repeated overshoot swings, not slow drift.\n\nWhat I accept from the round-1 critique:\n- Sensor span (item 1). I widen the outer sensors from x ±0.04 to ±0.06, with 0.03 m spacing. The outer sensor still overlaps tape when the line centre is about 0.07 m from the robot centre. This is a cheap margin for recovery, and it is within the contract limit of 0.08. I accept it as a cheap hedge, not as the proven cause.\n- kd (item 4). I lower kd from 0.7 to 0.4. The critique is right that a derivative on a quantised, noisy signal adds jitter, and I have no evidence that kd 0.7 damps anything. The 0.4 value is a compromise: it keeps some damping for the overshoot seen in the data, and it limits the derivative kick at line loss and reacquisition.\n- Speed (item 6). I keep base_speed 1.2 rather than raising it. The raced design's failure was leaving the track, not running out of time, and a lower speed gives the controller more time to correct. The 3 s finish is not yet tested, so this remains a risk. The completion_time metric will show whether 1.2 is too slow.\n\nWhat I partly accept or reject:\n- ki (item 3). I keep ki 0.1. The critique is right that its effect is small (integral at most 0.2 turn units, about 70 PWM). I keep it for the stated purpose of offsetting the seed-fixed motor mismatch, but I do not claim a measurable effect. The mismatch is not measured, so ki is a test, not a fix.\n- kp (item 2 and the evidence). I lower kp from 3.0 to 2.2 to reduce the overshoot swings that the oscillation metric shows. This is the one change I expect to matter most, because kp sets how far each sensor step turns the robot.\n- Sensor size and y (item 5). I keep size 0.016 and y 0.06. The critique's trade-off is real: a larger footprint flattens the response near centre. I accept that cost, because the raced design used the smaller footprint and still failed. Moving y forward from 0.04 to 0.06 gives the robot about 2 cm more lead, which I expect to help the overshoot, though the effect is not separable from the kp change in this race.\n- Iteration 2's raced design is treated as the baseline. Several changes are made at once, so this race tests the whole revised package, not each change alone. That is a known limit, and I accept it given the seven-iteration horizon.\n\nExpected result (guesses): fewer off-track exits, progress above 0.5 on the oval and clearly above 0.04 on the s-bend and slalom. Finishing is possible but uncertain at base 1.2. Diagnostics: if line_loss_events stays 0 and max_error stays near 0.06, the controller is still overshooting, so kp should drop further. If line_loss_events rises, the wider span or footprint is the cause. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.12, kd is adding jitter.",
